results.title: While standard SSMs were shown to be particularly powerful on signal processing tasks, their computation power is limited: the core sequential mechanism of S4 is equivalent to a convolution (filtering) [Li et al., 2022a]. This represents a drawback in challenging domains such as text and genetics, where the ability to select data efficiently in an input-dependent manner – i.e., perform content-based reasoning – is crucial (see [Wang et al., 2022, Fu et al., 2022, Arora et al., 2023]). Towards reaching this goal with recurrent models, various adaptations of S4 have been proposed in the last few months. Notably, Mamba [Gu and Dao, 2023] implements simple and efficient gating mechanisms on the S4 recurrence, unlocking input selectivity in the memory update. Mamba achieved state-of-the-art performance in various language modeling tasks while greatly improving the inference throughput. Similar ideas can be found in recent developments inspired by attention, such as RWKV [Peng et al., 2023], RetNet [Sun et al., 2023], Gated Linear Attention (GLA) [Yang et al., 2023], and HGRN2 [Qin et al., 2024]. Very recently, De et al. [2024] surpassed the performance of Mamba with a gated RNN architecture – Griffin – based on an improved version of the LRU [Orvieto et al., 2023a], and [Feng et al., 2024] introduced minimal versions of GRU and LSTM as gated SSMs.
